gaps.sentence: We'd better not ___ the neighbours again.
gaps.explanation: had better + bare infinitive (not comes after better): better not disturb.

gaps.sentence: He was made ___ for the damage to the rental car.
gaps.explanation: In the passive, 'be made to do' takes the to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: The box was heavy enough ___ two people.
gaps.explanation: adjective + enough + to-infinitive: heavy enough to need.

gaps.sentence: They agreed ___ the fence between the two gardens.
gaps.explanation: agree takes the to-infinitive: agreed to mend.

gaps.sentence: I didn't mean ___ you — it was a joke.
gaps.explanation: mean (= intend) takes the to-infinitive: didn't mean to upset. (mean + -ing = involve.)

gaps.sentence: I'd prefer ___ at home rather than go out.
gaps.explanation: would prefer + to-infinitive: I'd prefer to eat. (prefer + -ing for general likes.)

gaps.sentence: I regret ___ you that the flight has been cancelled.
gaps.explanation: regret + to-infinitive (formal announcements); regret + -ing = be sorry about the past.
